title: Can You Get PIP for Arthritis? UK Points & Evidence

direct_answer: Arthritis can qualify for Personal Independence Payment when it limits daily living or mobility, but diagnosis alone does not determine an award. DWP assesses 10 daily living and 2 mobility activities. Each component needs 8 points for the standard rate or 12 for enhanced, with tasks assessed for safety, acceptable standard, repetition and reasonable time.
author: Louis Maxwell
keywords: PIP for arthritis UK, PIP arthritis points, PIP evidence arthritis, arthritis benefits UK, PIP mobility arthritis
content:
What are the key points about PIP for arthritis?

  • PIP is based on how a condition affects specified activities, not on the arthritis diagnosis alone.
  • You need 8 points for the standard rate or 12 points for the enhanced rate of each component.
  • A task counts only if you can complete it safely, to an acceptable standard, repeatedly and within a reasonable time.
  • Explain fluctuating symptoms across the required period; a descriptor normally must apply on more than half the days.

Ready to apply? This page explains the criteria. Use our step-by-step PIP claim guide for arthritis for the claim process, forms, assessment and challenge routes.

Does arthritis automatically qualify for PIP?

No. Personal Independence Payment is decided by the functional effects of a long-term health condition or disability. Arthritis may lead to points when pain, stiffness, fatigue, reduced grip or restricted movement affects one or more assessed daily living or mobility activities.

Which activities does DWP assess for PIP?

DWP considers 10 daily living activities and 2 mobility activities. The descriptor that best reflects what you can do reliably determines the points for each activity.

ComponentActivities consideredAward thresholds
Daily livingPreparing food; taking nutrition; managing therapy; washing; toilet needs; dressing; communicating; reading; mixing with people; budgeting8 points standard; 12 points enhanced
MobilityPlanning and following journeys; moving around8 points standard; 12 points enhanced

What does completing a PIP activity reliably mean?

The assessment guide says you must be able to complete an activity safely, to an acceptable standard, repeatedly and within a reasonable time. Explain the consequences when any of these conditions is not met.

Safely
Without a risk of harm that is likely to occur, including risk during or after the activity.
Acceptable standard
Well enough for the activity's intended purpose.
Repeatedly
As often as the activity is reasonably required.
Reasonable time
No more than twice as long as a person without your condition would normally take.

How are arthritis flares and variable symptoms assessed?

DWP considers ability over a 12-month period rather than on one assessment day. A descriptor normally applies when it reflects your limitations on more than 50% of days. Describe the frequency and duration of better and worse days honestly, including after-effects and whether help or aids are needed.

What evidence can support a PIP claim for arthritis?

Evidence is most useful when it connects the condition to a specific assessed activity. Clinical evidence can confirm diagnosis and treatment, while a diary and concrete examples can show the help, aids, time, risk and after-effects involved.

EvidenceWhat it can demonstratePractical detail to include
Clinic, GP or therapy recordsDiagnosis, treatment, joint involvement and professional observationsUse existing relevant records; a diagnosis alone does not establish points
Medication or treatment listCurrent management and possible treatment burdenExplain support needed to manage therapy where relevant
Symptom and activity diaryFrequency, variability, time taken and after-effectsRecord representative better and worse days without exaggeration
Examples from daily lifeWhy an activity is unsafe, incomplete, slow or not repeatableName the activity, help or aid, outcome and recovery time

Can you claim PIP while working?

Yes. PIP is not means-tested and you can claim while working. Employment does not decide eligibility, although an assessor may ask how work activities compare with the limitations described in the claim. Explain any adjustments, equipment, assistance or recovery time that makes work possible.

Which claim route applies where I live?

Use GOV.UK for PIP claims in England and Wales and nidirect in Northern Ireland. In Scotland, new claims for this type of support are usually made through Adult Disability Payment. Check the official service for the country where you live before applying.

  • GOV.UK: How to claim PIP
  • nidirect: Personal Independence Payment
  • mygov.scot: Adult Disability Payment

What can you do if you disagree with a PIP decision?

The decision letter explains how and when to ask for mandatory reconsideration. If the decision remains unchanged, an appeal may be possible. Follow the deadline on the letter and consider help from Citizens Advice or a local welfare rights service; this guide is not legal advice.

Frequently asked questions

How many PIP points do you need for arthritis?

You need 8 points for the standard rate or 12 points for the enhanced rate of each component. Daily living and mobility are scored separately, so an award can cover one or both components.

Does arthritis automatically qualify for PIP?

No. PIP is based on the effect of your condition on specified activities, not the diagnosis itself. Arthritis may score points when its effects mean an activity cannot be completed reliably.

Can you get PIP for osteoarthritis or rheumatoid arthritis?

Either condition may support an award when the functional effects meet the assessment descriptors and points threshold. The arthritis type alone does not determine eligibility.

How does PIP assess arthritis flares?

DWP considers limitations across a 12-month period. A descriptor normally needs to apply on more than half the days, so explain how often flares occur, how long they last and how they affect each relevant activity.

Can you claim PIP for arthritis while working?

Yes. PIP is not means-tested and employment does not prevent a claim. Explain any workplace adjustments, help, equipment or recovery time that allows you to work despite the limitations described.

What evidence helps a PIP claim for arthritis?

Relevant clinical records can confirm diagnosis and treatment, while diaries and real examples can show functional impact. Link each item to a specific assessed activity and explain safety, standard, repetition and time.
